name: Chable Maroma
positioning: Chablé Maroma: a beachfront wellness resort of private pool villas on Maroma Beach in the Riviera Maya, set in a protected natural area
best_for: Travelers who want a private villa with its own pool steps from the Caribbean
Guests focused on spa and wellness rooted in Mayan tradition

facts.text: The resort is located directly on Maroma Beach, with immediate access to the Caribbean Sea.
The Reserve of Punta Maroma, where the resort sits, is 12 miles north of Playa del Carmen.
Chablé Maroma is set amidst a lush, protected natural area.
Villas have floor-to-ceiling windows and indoor-outdoor showers.
The Serenity Pool Villa has a private terrace with a heated plunge pool.
The three-bedroom Presidential Villa has a two-story layout with a plunge pool on each floor.
Bathrooms have separate his-and-hers water closets, and villas come with a Nespresso machine.
The wellness program includes spa treatments, fitness programs and mindfulness activities.
Dining centers on contemporary Mexican cuisine with fresh, local ingredients and coastal flavors.
Private transportation to and from Cancun International Airport can be arranged.
Nearby attractions include Playa del Carmen, cenotes and Mayan archaeological sites such as Tulum and Cobá.
The hotel works with a local dive outfit, and there is coral and reef life about 30 minutes offshore.

highlights.text: The resort has a 650-foot private beach.
Each villa has a private outdoor terrace and pool.
Interior designer Paulina Morán designed the villas, with nature and Mexican artisanal traditions as a central focus.
Treetop Pool Villas are elevated on a second-floor perch, each with a private plunge pool.
The full-service spa focuses on holistic well-being, and its experience is deeply rooted in Mayan tradition.

considerations.text: Chablé Maroma is not an all-inclusive resort; guests customize dining, wellness and activities.
Families are welcome, but the resort is especially suited to travelers looking for tranquility and wellness-oriented stays.
